this_numpy_implementation.derivation: 5 ufunc passes over the block: add(up,down)->d = 8+8+8, add(d,left) = 8+8+8, add(d,right) = 8+8+8, multiply(d,.25) = 8+8 -> 104 B/point (neighbour rows reuse cache, write-allocate ignored)

machine.bandwidth_source: 1 channel(s) x 4800 MT/s x 8 B (from DIMM info)

working_set.note: Strong-scaling grids fit in L3, so traffic is served partly by the LLC rather than DRAM; the kernel is still bandwidth-bound (LLC bandwidth instead of DRAM bandwidth).

conclusion: AI = 0.167 FLOP/B (ideal) and 0.038 FLOP/B (numpy) are far below the ridge point 24.19 FLOP/B, so the stencil sits on the sloped (bandwidth) part of the roofline: adding cores helps only until the memory subsystem saturates, which is what limits the strong-scaling efficiency.
